found_by: agent, at $0, while building the screening session's launcher
severity: scientific. It is not an engineering failure and was not repaired autonomously.
_one_line: D1's design declares its control arm to be the arm C1 measured and BEAT, and C1's measured delta between the two arms is larger than the SESOI D1's decision rule tests against.

declared_by_the_design.what_it_actually_is: C1's INCUMBENT arm — attention.weight_proxy_v0 on calib.none@v1 — which is the Phase-A/B winner C1 was testing a replacement for

the_arm_that_actually_stands.why: C1's verdict was GO at a pooled delta of +0.013725490196078431 against a SESOI of 0.010, which promotes the treatment arm

why_it_matters.the_arithmetic: C1's own measured delta between these two arms is +0.013725. The D-series SESOI is 0.010. A candidate measured against the beaten arm is therefore credited with an effect LARGER than the amount the decision rule tests for.
why_it_matters.the_consequence: This does not add noise to a D1 result; it lowers the bar by more than the bar. All four candidates could clear a SESOI they do not reach, and the screening rung would rank them on a quantity inflated identically for every arm — so even the RANKING's claim to be a paired comparison against the incumbent would be false.
why_it_matters.the_estimand_it_breaks: the frozen decision rule's estimand is the prompt-mean of the seed-mean paired difference (candidate - B). If the control is not B, that difference estimates nothing the design named.

the_decision_required.question: Is D1's control arm the standing incumbent (C1's treatment, 53e30566) — correcting the design — or was the pre-C1 arm (c313d1b4) deliberately chosen?
the_decision_required.why_it_is_not_an_autonomous_repair: AGENTS.md P12.1 stops autonomous continuation at 'changing arms, seeds, datasets, scoring or decision rules'. Correcting the control changes the ARMS, and because `incumbent` is inside `scientific_preimage` it also moves `design_hash` and therefore the derived screening and confirmation SEEDS.

design_hash.note: both differ from the 83cd49ff... the completed search ran under; design_hash has already moved three times across D1's own runs and no committed record is invalidated by another move

what_moves_if_it_is_corrected.seeds: the screening and confirmation seeds are SHA256(design_hash + ':phase-d1:<rung>-seed:' + i), so they are redrawn. This is harmless NOW and only now: C0 requires them materialized and hash-bound in an execution preregistration BEFORE any candidate behavioural result exists, and none exists.
what_moves_if_it_is_corrected.how_B_is_sourced: the promoted arm has NO search state id — it was built as a fixed path — so it cannot come from a state-id directory, and its bytes are not on the development host. It is materialized ON THE POD from `phase_c2.baseline.frozen_baseline_spec`, the one owner of that construction, which is what C2's and C3's behavioural sessions did and what the screening cell's `parent_replay_and_incumbent_rebuild` overhead already prices.
what_does_NOT_move: the candidate field — the Top-4 retention decision is unaffected, B was never a search candidate

a_second_finding_in_the_same_decision.what: the screening session as priced does not fund materializing the four CANDIDATES on the pod.
a_second_finding_in_the_same_decision.detail: budget.chain.sessions.screening is 10 probes x 89.516 min plus a 104-minute overhead whose arm term is `parent_replay_and_incumbent_rebuild: 22.0` — one rebuild, modelled on C3, which had one. D1 screening has five arms. The four candidates' 1.2 GiB checkpoints cannot be shipped to a pod (scp has a hardcoded 600 s per-asset timeout against a 0.72 MB/s uplink; the hub relay has ~1.756 GiB of private-storage headroom), so they are materialized on the pod along digest-pinned fixed paths — the mechanism the finalist rematerialization campaign proved by reproducing q2 and q4 byte-for-byte, at 963.2 s and 1280.3 s on an L40S.
a_second_finding_in_the_same_decision.consequence: a re-price is owed before the screening authorization is issued. It is a derivation from the design's own cost model, not a new estimate, and the $30 per-session envelope and the $68.7925 remaining formal allowance both have room — but the priced figure the authorization binds must be the one that covers the work.
a_second_finding_in_the_same_decision.why_it_is_recorded_here: it touches the same decision: WHICH checkpoint B is determines whether B is one of the materializations or a staged input.

priced_now.arm_term_in_the_overhead: parent_replay_and_incumbent_rebuild: 22.0 min — ONE rebuild, from C3's component table, and C3 had one arm to rebuild

measured_basis.what: the finalist rematerialization campaign's r7, on the same L40S, along the same digest-pinned fixed paths
measured_basis.note: q1 and q3 carry the same operator multiset in a different order, so the same per-leaf figure bounds them

worst_observation_bound.what: the search's own worst `operator_seconds` per IMPLEMENTATION, the basis the design's cost model uses
worst_observation_bound.why_it_overstates_here: it is dominated by DEPTH's worst observation, which was at the ROOT; all four candidate paths run DEPTH at a non-root position, which is why the two MEASURED leaves came in at 16.05 and 21.34 min against a 43.61-min bound

the_arithmetic.the_delta_to_price: +85 min on the measured basis, +196 min at the worst-observation bound, against a 1267.71-min ceiling. At $1.09/h plus the disk term that is roughly +$1.55 to +$3.60, moving the screening ceiling to about $25-$27 — inside the $30 per-session envelope, and inside the $68.7925 remaining formal allowance.
the_arithmetic.not_a_re_estimate: every figure above is READ from a record: the priced cell from the design, the per-leaf measurement from the replay campaign's closeout, the per-implementation worsts from the search's own telemetry via replay_specs.worst_seconds_by_impl(). The re-price is a derivation through search_space.behavioural_cost, not a new estimate.

resolution.decision: The standing incumbent B is C1's PROMOTED TREATMENT, artifact_digest 53e30566c5f795f1870d76c1fa6a970ddc507fa5459047f3010ffab8aa890342. NOT c313d1b4081b9a3b410dddf7a29ebcaad8dd0759179d51e1d761238c1743a2a6.
resolution._not_a_new_scientific_choice: the maintainer's decision states this explicitly: repository evidence already established it. c1_arm_identities.json identifies c313d1b4... as C1's incumbent/weight-proxy arm and 53e30566... as its treatment/activation-importance arm; C1 returned GO; Phase-C2 defines B_ARTIFACT_DIGEST = 53e30566... and describes B as 'the frozen C1 treatment'. The old D1 identity is therefore a DEFECT, and this is its mechanical correction rather than a protocol change.
what_was_changed: write_d1_design.py :: the typed INCUMBENT_STATE_ID/INCUMBENT_DIGEST constants are DELETED. `incumbent()` derives the block from phase_d_series.incumbent.standing_incumbent, which reads C1's verdict and C1's measured arm identities, and emits all four content identities plus the construction facts.
the design's `incumbent.state_id` is now null, which is the arm's own shape: the promoted arm was built as a FIXED PATH and c1_arm_identities records state_id: null for it.

behavioural.py :: ARM_SOURCES no longer carries a B entry (there is no state-id directory and its bytes are not on this host); `Arm` gained `identities` and `construction`; `arms()` assembles B as a spec-materialized arm; `require_arms_present` verifies candidates by hashing their bytes and B by comparing its construction spec's four pins against the design.
search_space.py :: the arm-materialization cost left the FIXED session overhead and became a per-arm term. See `the_second_finding_resolution`.
resolution.the_blocker_is_kept_not_deleted: `incumbent identity` stays in BLOCKER_SPECS and `arms()` keeps its refusal. The design is a FILE and the derivation is code, so the check compares the document against the owner: an edited design, or a later round that promoted something else without this document following, is still refused. The regression drives the refusal through the exact historical value rather than leaving it unexercised now that it passes.

design_hash.note: the shape of the `incumbent` block changed as well as its value -- four content identities and the construction facts replace a state id and a 12-hex prefix -- so the hash is not the bd4c7d4a... projected from a value-only change.

seeds_rebound.rule: SHA256(design_hash + ':phase-d1:<rung>-seed:' + i) mod 2**31, advancing past every excluded seed
seeds_rebound._why_this_is_valid: C0 requires the seeds materialized and hash-bound BEFORE any candidate behavioural result exists, and none exists: no D1 probe has been trained, no authorization has been issued and no pod has been created. The rebinding is prospective.
seeds_rebound._still_owed: an execution preregistration that hash-binds these values must be written before the first behavioural launch. It does not exist yet and this record does not stand in for it.

the_second_finding_resolution.what_was_wrong: `parent_replay_and_incumbent_rebuild: 22.0` sat in BEHAVIOURAL_SESSION_MINUTES, a FIXED per-session overhead. It is the cost of materializing ONE arm -- C3's figure, for a session that had one arm. D1 screening has five, so the priced session funded a fifth of the arm materialization it requires.
the_second_finding_resolution.what_was_changed: the term left the overhead and became ARM_MATERIALIZATION_MINUTES = 22.0, multiplied by a REQUIRED `n_arms` argument on `behavioural_cost`. `chain_cost` and `designs()` thread the two rungs' arm counts, and the overrun factor still applies to the train+eval block only -- materialization is a digest-pinned replay already carried at a bound.
the_second_finding_resolution.why_22_minutes: C3's own component figure for exactly this operation, and the D1 finalist rematerialization campaign then MEASURED two of these four candidate paths end to end on the same L40S at 963.2 s (16.05 min) and 1280.3 s (21.34 min), both inside it. The bound that contains the measurements is what is priced.
the_second_finding_resolution.fits: screening $25.0053 against the $30.0000 per-session envelope; chain $61.6975 against $68.7925 of remaining formal allowance. No limit is approached and no funding decision is implied.
the_second_finding_resolution._pricing_repair_not_execution: no authorization was issued, no pod was created and no screening or confirmation work ran.

a_third_repair_found_while_closing.what: `phase_d_series/source_evidence.py` produced a HASH-SEED DEPENDENT record, so `autoinit_d_series_source_evidence.json` could not regenerate identically and its own test could only pass when the ambient PYTHONHASHSEED matched the one in use when it was written.
a_third_repair_found_while_closing.found_by: the test was red before this round and the red was attributed, not inherited: none of this round's files feeds that generator, so it was diagnosed rather than assumed related
the_two_causes: `near_duplicate_screen` chose each prompt's `rare_tokens` rarest words with `sorted(t, key=df.__getitem__)` over a frozenset, so ties in document frequency were broken by SET ITERATION ORDER. Different seeds indexed and queried different tokens, so different candidates were compared at all.

`bare_problem_screen` built `by_hash` from a set and took the first STRICT maximum, so a candidate's `resembles_consumed_task_id` came back as 17 at one seed and 458 at another -- a review surface naming two different prompts as the thing a candidate resembles.
a_third_repair_found_while_closing.the_fix: total orders: `(df[w], w)` for the rare-token choice, `sorted(reserved)` and `sorted(keys)` for the index builds, `sorted(by_hash.items())` for the partner scan, and `(-jaccard, candidate_task_id)` for the review-list sort. Verified stable across PYTHONHASHSEED 1, 7 and 13 -- one digest.
